full_judgment: 2. Facts leading to this Rule are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 89 of 1983 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna against the defendant-opposite parties for declaration of title to the suit land described in the schedule to the plaint. The land measuring a total of 30.66 acres of CS Khatian Nos. 54 and 55 to 56 originally belonged to one Banikanti Roy. During RS operation those lands were recorded in RS Khatian Nos. 184, 185 and 186. The land of RS Khatian No.184 belonged to Khirod, Angod, Binoy, Dukhiram, Jogendra Math, Anania, Surendra, Soitya Bala, Trishnaboti, Aswini, Dhoru, Gadadhar, Sipin and Meneka Sundari as tenants. Due to non-payment of rent government started a certificate case No.546 KM/1955-56 and in that certificate case the entire land of RS Khatian No.184 was put to auction. The plaintiff for the purpose of purchasing the said land in auction sent his brother-in-law Krishnapada Mondal to purchase it in auction in the name of the plaintiff but Krishnapada purchased the same in his own name to the extent of 10 anna share and other 6 anna share was purchased by some other persons. The auction sale took place on 25-1-1956 and was confirmed on 3-4-1956 and that Krishnapada took delivery of possession of the land on behalf of the plaintiff and since then the plaintiff has been possessing the auction-purchased land. During SA operation the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of ex-tenants. Thereafter, one Ananta and Trishnaboti filed Miscellaneous Case No. 194 of 1961-62 to set aside the auction sale but this Miscellaneous case ended in compromise and that the auction sale to the extent of 3.22 acres of land was set aside and the auction to the extent of 5.74 acres of land was confirmed, out of which the plaintiffs 10 annas share measuring 3.60 acres of land remained in tact. The plaintiff has been possessing this land through borgadars and paid rent. The plaintiff was the real purchaser-owner of the suit land and Krishnapada was simply his benamdar. Thereafter, this Krishnapada sold the land in favour of defendants on 13-3-1983. This sale to the defendants is a collusive sale and that the defendants did not get title or possession by their purchase. This sale clouded the plaintiff's title and hence the plaintiff filed the suit as aforesaid.
